properties.address: 1 W Register St, Edinburgh EH2 2AA, UK

properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean strata comprise Carboniferous sedimentary sandstone and siltstone bedrock of the Inverclyde Group, overlain by dense glacial till. Primary structural masonry consists of local pale buff-grey Craigleith and Hailes sandstones bonded with traditional non-hydraulic lime-sand mortars. Ground conditions feature engineered urban sub-base over drained historic glacial clay deposits.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Mature urban parkland perimeter populated by *Acer pseudoplatanus* (sycamore), *Tilia × europaea* (common lime), and *Betula pendula* (silver birch). Late September phenology: full canopy density exhibiting initial autumn chlorosis, yellowing outer margins, and sporadic early leaf litter across turf and gravel circuits.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical urban square anchored by the 45-metre fluted Craigleith sandstone Melville Monument, featuring a stepped pedestal and Roman Doric column crowned with a colossal stone statue. Surrounding perimeter consists of 4-to-6-storey Georgian and Victorian commercial palazzo blocks and townhouses: rusticated ashlar ground tiers, regularized 6-over-6 and 2-over-2 timber sash-and-case fenestration grids, dentiled eaves cornices, and Ballachulish slate mansard roofs punctuated by dressed ashlar chimney stacks. Modern mid-to-late 20th-century infill blocks feature rectified concrete frames and modular stone veneer grid facades.
